verses.zh: 七日的头一日，黎明的时候，那些妇女带着所预备的香料来到坟墓前，
verses.en: Now on the first day[NOTE:1] of the week, at early dawn, the women[NOTE:2] went to the tomb, taking the aromatic spices[NOTE:3] they had prepared.
notes: The first day of the week is the day after the Sabbath.
Grk “they”; the referent (the women mentioned in 23:55) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
On this term see BDAG 140-41 s.v. ἄρωμα. See also the note on “aromatic spices” in 23:56.

verses.zh: 看见石头已经从坟墓滚开了，
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] found that the stone had been rolled away from the tomb,[NOTE:2]
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

Luke tells the story of the empty tomb with little drama. He simply notes that when they arrived the stone had been rolled away in a position where the tomb could be entered. This large stone was often placed in a channel so that it could be easily moved by rolling it aside. The other possibility is that it was merely placed over the opening in a position from which it had now been moved.

verses.zh: 她们就进去，只是不见主耶稣的身体。
verses.en: but when they went in, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.[NOTE:1]
notes: What they found was not what they expected—an empty tomb.tc The translation follows the much better attested longer reading here, “body of the Lord Jesus” (found in {P75 א A B C L W Θ Ψ ƒ1,13 33 565 700 M}), rather than simply “the body” (found in D it) or “the body of Jesus” (found in 579 1241). Further, although this is the only time that “Lord Jesus” occurs in Luke, it seems to be Luke’s normal designation for the Lord after his resurrection (note the many references to Christ in this manner in Acts, e.g., 1:21; 4:33; 7:59; 8:16; 11:17; 15:11; 16:31; 19:5; 20:21; 28:31). Although such a longer reading as this would normally be suspect, in this case some scribes, accustomed to Luke’s more abbreviated style, did not take the resurrection into account.

verses.zh: 正在猜疑之间，忽然有两个人站在旁边，衣服放光。
verses.en: While[NOTE:1] they were perplexed[NOTE:2] about this, suddenly[NOTE:3] two men stood beside them in dazzling[NOTE:4] attire.
notes: Grk “And it happened that while.” The introductory phrase ἐγένετο (egeneto, “it happened that”), common in Luke (69 times) and Acts (54 times), is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated. Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Or “bewildered.” The term refers to a high state of confusion and anxiety.
Grk “behold.”
The brilliantly shining clothing (dazzling attire) points to the fact that these are angels (see 24:23).

verses.zh: 妇女们惊怕，将脸伏地。那两个人就对她们说：「为甚么在死人中找活人呢？
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] women[NOTE:2] were terribly frightened[NOTE:3] and bowed[NOTE:4] their faces to the ground, but the men said to them, “Why do you look for the living[NOTE:5] among the dead?
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Grk “they”; the referent (the women) has been specified in the translation for clarity (the same has been done in v. 8).
Or “They were extremely afraid.”
Bowed their faces to the ground. Such respect for angels is common: Dan 7:28; 10:9, 15.
By referring to Jesus as the living, the angels make it clear that he is alive. There should be no surprise.

verses.zh: 他不在这里，已经复活了。当记念他还在加利利的时候怎样告诉你们，
verses.en: He is not here, but has been raised![NOTE:1] Remember how he told you, while he was still in Galilee,[NOTE:2]
notes: The verb here is passive (ἠγέρθη, ēgerthē). This “divine passive” (see ExSyn 437-38) points to the fact that Jesus was raised by God, and such activity by God is a consistent Lukan theological emphasis: Luke 20:37; 24:34; Acts 3:15; 4:10; 5:30; 10:40; 13:30, 37. A passive construction is also used to refer to Jesus’ exaltation: Luke 24:51; Acts 1:11, 22. tc The phrase “He is not here, but has been raised” is omitted by a few mss (D it), but it has wide ms support and differs slightly from the similar statement in Matt 28:6 and Mark 16:6. Although NA28 places the phrase at the beginning of v. 6, as do most modern English translations, it is omitted from the RSV and placed at the end of v. 5 in the NRSV.
While he was still in Galilee looks back to the beginning of Jesus’ ministry. So the point is that this was announced long ago, and should come as no surprise.

verses.zh: 说：『人子必须被交在罪人手里，钉在十字架上，第三日复活。』」
verses.en: that[NOTE:1] the Son of Man must be delivered[NOTE:2] into the hands of sinful men,[NOTE:3] and be crucified,[NOTE:4] and on the third day rise again.”[NOTE:5]
notes: Grk “saying that,” but this would be redundant in English. Although the translation represents this sentence as indirect discourse, the Greek could equally be taken as direct discourse: “Remember how he told you, while he was still in Galilee: ‘the Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again.’”

Because in the historical context the individuals who were primarily responsible for the death of Jesus (the Jewish leadership in Jerusalem in Luke’s view [see Luke 9:22]) would have been men, the translation “sinful men” for ἀνθρώπων ἁμαρτωλῶν (anthrōpōn hamartōlōn) is retained here.
See the note on crucify in 23:21.
Here the infinitive ἀναστῆναι (anastēnai) is active rather than passive.

verses.zh: 她们就想起耶稣的话来，
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] the women remembered his words,[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
On his words see Luke 9:22.

verses.zh: 便从坟墓那里回去，把这一切的事告诉十一个使徒和其余的人。
verses.en: and when they returned from the tomb, they told all these things to the eleven[NOTE:1] and to all the rest.
notes: Judas is now absent and “the twelve” have now become “the eleven.” Other disciples are also gathered with the remaining eleven.

verses.zh: 那告诉使徒的就是抹大拉的马利亚和约亚拿，并雅各的母亲马利亚，还有与她们在一处的妇女。
verses.en: Now it was Mary Magdalene,[NOTE:1] Joanna,[NOTE:2] Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told these things to the apostles.
notes: Mary Magdalene is always noted first in the appearance lists in the gospels. It is unusual that the first appearance would involve women as in this culture their role as witnesses would not be well accepted. It is a sign of the veracity of the account because if an ancient were to create such a story he would never have it start with women.
On Joanna see Luke 8:1-3.

verses.zh: 她们这些话，使徒以为是胡言，就不相信。
verses.en: But these words seemed like pure nonsense[NOTE:1] to them, and they did not believe them.
notes: The term pure nonsense can describe idle talk or a tale. The point is important, since the disciples reacted with disbelief that a resurrection was possible. Sometimes it is thought the ancients were gullible enough to believe anything. But these disciples needed convincing about the resurrection.

verses.zh: 彼得起来，跑到坟墓前，低头往里看，见细麻布独在一处，就回去了，心里希奇所成的事。
verses.en: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb.[NOTE:1] He bent down[NOTE:2] and saw only the strips of linen cloth;[NOTE:3] then he went home,[NOTE:4] wondering[NOTE:5] what had happened.[NOTE:6]
notes: While the others dismissed the report of the women, Peter got up and ran to the tomb, for he had learned to believe in what the Lord had said.
In most instances the entrance to such tombs was less than 3 ft (1 m) high, so that an adult would have to bend down and practically crawl inside.
In the NT this term is used only for strips of cloth used to wrap a body for burial (LN 6.154; BDAG 693 s.v. ὀθόνιον).

Or “went away, wondering to himself.” The prepositional phrase πρὸς ἑαυτόν (pros heauton) can be understood with the preceding verb ἀπῆλθεν (apēlthen) or with the following participle θαυμάζων (thaumazōn), but it more likely belongs with the former (cf. John 20:10, where the phrase can only refer to the verb).
Peter’s wondering was not a lack of faith, but struggling in an attempt to understand what could have happened.

Some Western mss (D it) lack 24:12. The verse has been called a Western noninterpolation, meaning that it reflects a shorter authentic reading in D and other Western witnesses. Many regard all such shorter readings as original (the verse is omitted in the RSV), but the ms evidence for omission is far too slight for the verse to be rejected as secondary. It is included in P75 and the rest of the ms tradition.

verses.zh: 正当那日，门徒中有两个人往一个村子去；这村子名叫以马忤斯，离耶路撒冷约有二十五里。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] that very day two of them[NOTE:2] were on their way to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles[NOTE:3] from Jerusalem.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “And behold.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic. The Greek word ἰδού (idou) at the beginning of this statement has not been translated because it has no exact English equivalent here, but adds interest and emphasis (BDAG 468 s.v. 1).
These are disciples as they know about the empty tomb and do not know what to make of it all.
Grk “sixty stades” or about 11 kilometers. A stade (στάδιον, stadion) was a unit of distance about 607 feet (185 meters) long.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 他们彼此谈论所遇见的这一切事。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] were talking to each other about all the things that had happened.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

verses.zh: 正谈论相问的时候，耶稣亲自就近他们，和他们同行；
verses.en: While[NOTE:1] they were talking and debating[NOTE:2] these things,[NOTE:3] Jesus himself approached and began to accompany them
notes: Grk “And it happened that while.” The introductory phrase ἐγένετο (egeneto, “it happened that”), common in Luke (69 times) and Acts (54 times), is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated. Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
This term suggests emotional dialogue and can thus be translated “debated.”
The phrase “these things” is not in the Greek text, but is implied. Direct objects were frequently omitted in Greek when clear from the context.

verses.zh: 只是他们的眼睛迷糊了，不认识他。
verses.en: (but their eyes were kept[NOTE:1] from recognizing[NOTE:2] him).[NOTE:3]
notes: The two disciples will not be allowed to recognize Jesus until v. 31.
This is an epexegetical (i.e., explanatory) infinitive in Greek.
This parenthetical remark by the author is necessary so the reader will understand the account.

verses.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「你们走路彼此谈论的是甚么事呢？」他们就站住，脸上带着愁容。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he said to them, “What are these matters[NOTE:2] you are discussing so intently[NOTE:3] as you walk along?” And they stood still, looking sad.
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “words,” but the term λόγος (logos) can refer to “matters” rather than only “words” (BDAG 600 s.v. 1.a.ε).

“Discussing so intently” translates the reciprocal idea conveyed by πρὸς ἀλλήλους (pros allēlous). The term ἀντιβάλλω (antiballō), used only here in the NT, has the nuance of “arguing” or “debating” a point (the English idiom “to exchange words” also comes close).

verses.zh: 二人中有一个名叫革流巴的回答说：「你在耶路撒冷作客，还不知道这几天在那里所出的事吗？」
verses.en: Then one of them, named Cleopas, answered him,[NOTE:1] “Are you the only visitor to Jerusalem who doesn’t know[NOTE:2] the things that have happened there[NOTE:3] in these days?”
notes: Grk “answering him, said.” This is redundant in English and has been simplified in the translation.

There is irony and almost a sense of mocking disbelief as the question “Are you the only visitor to Jerusalem who doesn’t know the things that have happened there in these days?” comes to Jesus, but, of course, the readers know what the travelers do not.
Grk “in it” (referring to the city of Jerusalem).

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「甚么事呢？」他们说：「就是拿撒勒人耶稣的事。他是个先知，在　神和众百姓面前，说话行事都有大能。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] said to them, “What things?” “The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene,” they replied, “a man[NOTE:2] who, with his powerful deeds and words, proved to be a prophet[NOTE:3] before God and all the people;
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
This translates the Greek term ἀνήρ (anēr).
The role of Jesus as prophet is a function Luke frequently mentions: 4:25-27; 9:35; 13:31-35.

verses.zh: 祭司长和我们的官府竟把他解去，定了死罪，钉在十字架上。
verses.en: and how our chief priests and leaders handed him over[NOTE:1] to be condemned to death, and crucified[NOTE:2] him.
notes: Handed him over is another summary of the passion like Luke 9:22.
See the note on crucify in 23:21.

verses.zh: 但我们素来所盼望、要赎以色列民的就是他！不但如此，而且这事成就，现在已经三天了。
verses.en: But we had hoped[NOTE:1] that he was the one who was going to redeem[NOTE:2] Israel. Not only this, but it is now the third day since these things happened.
notes: The imperfect verb looks back to the view that they held during Jesus’ past ministry.
Their messianic hope concerning Jesus is expressed by the phrase who was going to redeem Israel.

verses.zh: 再者，我们中间有几个妇女使我们惊奇；她们清早到了坟墓那里，
verses.en: Furthermore, some women of our group amazed us.[NOTE:1] They[NOTE:2] were at the tomb early this morning,
notes: The account in 24:1-12 is repeated here, and it is clear that the other disciples were not convinced by the women, but could not explain the events either.
In the Greek text this is a continuation of the previous sentence, but because of the length and complexity of the construction a new sentence was started here in the translation.

verses.zh: 不见他的身体，就回来告诉我们，说看见了天使显现，说他活了。
verses.en: and when they did not find his body, they came back and said they had seen a vision of angels,[NOTE:1] who said he was alive.
notes: The men in dazzling attire mentioned in v. 4 are identified as angels here.

verses.zh: 又有我们的几个人往坟墓那里去，所遇见的正如妇女们所说的，只是没有看见他。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] some of those who were with us went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see him.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Here the pronoun αὐτόν (auton), referring to Jesus, is in an emphatic position. The one thing they lacked was solid evidence that he was alive.

verses.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「无知的人哪，先知所说的一切话，你们的心信得太迟钝了。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] he said to them, “You[NOTE:2] foolish people[NOTE:3]—how slow of heart[NOTE:4] to believe[NOTE:5] all that the prophets have spoken!
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the disciples’ inability to believe in Jesus’ resurrection.
Grk “O,” an interjection used both in address and emotion (BDAG 1101 s.v. 1).
The word “people” is not in the Greek text, but is supplied to complete the interjection.
The rebuke is for failure to believe the promise of scripture, a theme that will appear in vv. 43-47 as well.
On the syntax of this infinitival construction, see BDAG 364-65 s.v. ἐπί 6.b.

verses.zh: 基督这样受害，又进入他的荣耀，岂不是应当的吗？」
verses.en: Wasn’t[NOTE:1] it necessary[NOTE:2] for the Christ[NOTE:3] to suffer these things and enter into his glory?”
notes: This Greek particle (οὐχί, ouchi) expects a positive reply.
The statement Wasn’t it necessary is a reference to the design of God’s plan (see Luke 24:7). Suffering must precede glory (see Luke 17:25).
See the note on Christ in 2:11.tn Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”

verses.zh: 于是从摩西和众先知起，凡经上所指着自己的话都给他们讲解明白了。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] beginning with Moses and all the prophets,[NOTE:2] he interpreted to them the things written about[NOTE:3] himself in all the scriptures.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
The reference to Moses and all the prophets is a way to say the promise of Messiah runs throughout OT scripture from first to last.

Or “regarding,” “concerning.” “Written” is implied by the mention of the scriptures in context; “said” could also be used here, referring to the original utterances, but by now these things had been committed to writing.

verses.zh: 将近他们所去的村子，耶稣好像还要往前行，
verses.en: So they approached the village where they were going. He acted as though he wanted to go farther,[NOTE:1]
notes: He acted as though he wanted to go farther. This is written in a way that gives the impression Jesus knew they would ask him to stay.

verses.zh: 他们却强留他，说：「时候晚了，日头已经平西了，请你同我们住下吧！」耶稣就进去，要同他们住下。
verses.en: but they urged him,[NOTE:1] “Stay with us because it is getting toward evening and the day is almost done.” So[NOTE:2] he went in to stay with them.
notes: Grk “urged him, saying.” The participle λέγοντες (legontes, “saying”) has not been translated because it is redundant in contemporary English.
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the disciples’ request.

verses.zh: 到了坐席的时候，耶稣拿起饼来，祝谢了，擘开，递给他们。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] he had taken his place at the table[NOTE:2] with them, he took the bread, blessed and broke it,[NOTE:3] and gave it to them.
notes: Grk “And it happened that when.” The introductory phrase ἐγένετο (egeneto, “it happened that”), common in Luke (69 times) and Acts (54 times), is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated. Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

Grk “had reclined at table,” as 1st century middle eastern meals were not eaten while sitting at a table, but while reclining on one’s side on the floor with the head closest to the low table and the feet farthest away.
The pronoun “it” is not in the Greek text here or in the following clause, but is implied. Direct objects were frequently omitted in Greek when clear from the context.

verses.zh: 他们的眼睛明亮了，这才认出他来。忽然耶稣不见了。
verses.en: At this point[NOTE:1] their eyes were opened and they recognized[NOTE:2] him.[NOTE:3] Then[NOTE:4] he vanished out of their sight.
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “At this point” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative. “Then,” which is normally used to indicate this, would be redundant with the following clause.
They recognized him. Other than this cryptic remark, it is not told how the two disciples were now able to recognize Jesus.
This pronoun is somewhat emphatic.
This translates a καί (kai, “and”) that has clear sequential force.

verses.zh: 他们彼此说：「在路上，他和我们说话，给我们讲解圣经的时候，我们的心岂不是火热的吗？」
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] said to each other, “Didn’t[NOTE:2] our hearts[NOTE:3] burn within us[NOTE:4] while he was speaking with us on the road, while he was explaining[NOTE:5] the scriptures to us?”
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
This question uses a Greek particle (οὐχί, ouchi) that expects a positive reply.
This is a collective singular use of the term καρδία (kardia), so each of their hearts were burning, a reference itself to the intense emotion of their response.

Even though it is most likely not original (see tc note above), the phrase within us has been included in the translation for clarity.tc ‡ Most mss have the phrase ἐν ἡμῖν (en hēmin, “within us”) after οὐχὶ ἡ καρδία ἡμῶν καιομένη ἦν (ouchi hē kardia hēmōn kaiomenē ēn, “Didn’t our hearts burn”). The phrase “within us” is lacking in some early mss (P75 B D c e sys,c). These early witnesses could have overlooked the words, since there are several occurrences of ἡμῖν in the context. But it seems likely that other scribes wanted to clarify the abrupt expression “Didn’t our hearts burn,” even as the translation has done here. NA28 includes the words in brackets, indicating doubts as to their authenticity.
Grk “opening” (cf. Acts 17:3).

verses.zh: 他们就立时起身，回耶路撒冷去，正遇见十一个使徒和他们的同人聚集在一处，
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] they got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem.[NOTE:2] They[NOTE:3] found the eleven and those with them gathered together
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the Lord’s appearance to them.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

verses.zh: 说：「主果然复活，已经现给西门看了。」
verses.en: and[NOTE:1] saying, “The Lord has really risen and has appeared to Simon!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Here the word “and” has been supplied to make it clear that the disciples who had been to Emmaus found the eleven plus the others gathered and saying this.
The Lord…has appeared to Simon. Jesus had made another appearance besides the one on the road. The excitement was rising. Simon refers to Simon Peter.

verses.zh: 两个人就把路上所遇见，和擘饼的时候怎么被他们认出来的事，都述说了一遍。
verses.en: Then they told what had happened on the road,[NOTE:1] and how they recognized him[NOTE:2] when he broke the bread.
notes: Now with the recounting of what had happened on the road two sets of witnesses corroborate the women’s report.

Grk “how he was made known to them”; or “how he was recognized by them.” Here the passive construction has been converted to an active one in the translation in keeping with contemporary English style.

verses.zh: 正说这话的时候，耶稣亲自站在他们当中，说：「愿你们平安！」
verses.en: While they were saying these things, Jesus[NOTE:1] himself stood among them and said to them, “Peace be with you.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The words “and said to them, ‘Peace be with you’” are lacking in some Western mss (D it). But the clause is otherwise well attested, being found in P75 and the rest of the ms tradition, and should be considered an original part of Luke.

verses.zh: 他们却惊慌害怕，以为所看见的是魂。
verses.en: But they were startled and terrified, thinking[NOTE:1] they saw a ghost.[NOTE:2]
notes: The disciples were still not comfortable at this point thinking that this could be Jesus raised from the dead. Instead they thought they saw a spirit.

This is not a reference to “a phantom” as read by the Western ms D. For πνεῦμα (pneuma) having the force of “ghost,” or “an independent noncorporeal being, in contrast to a being that can be perceived by the physical senses,” see BDAG 833-34 s.v. πνεῦμα 4.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「你们为甚么愁烦？为甚么心里起疑念呢？
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he said to them, “Why are you frightened,[NOTE:2] and why do doubts[NOTE:3] arise in your hearts?
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Or “disturbed,” “troubled.”

Jesus calls the disciples to faith with a gentle rebuke about doubts and a gracious invitation to see for themselves the evidence of his resurrection.tn The expression here is an idiom; see BDAG 58 s.v. ἀναβαίνω 2. Here καρδία (kardia) is a collective singular; the expression has been translated as plural in English.

verses.zh: 你们看我的手，我的脚，就知道实在是我了。摸我看看！魂无骨无肉，你们看，我是有的。」
verses.en: Look at my hands and my feet; it’s me![NOTE:1] Touch me and see; a ghost[NOTE:2] does not have flesh and bones like you see I have.”
notes: Grk “that it is I myself.”
See tc note on “ghost” in v. 37.

verses.zh: 说了这话，就把手和脚给他们看。
verses.en: When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.[NOTE:1]
notes: Some Western mss (D it) lack 24:40. However, it is present in all other mss, including P75, and should thus be regarded as an original part of Luke’s Gospel.

verses.zh: 他们正喜得不敢信，并且希奇；耶稣就说：「你们这里有甚么吃的没有？」
verses.en: And while they still could not believe it[NOTE:1] (because of their joy) and were amazed,[NOTE:2] he said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”[NOTE:3]
notes: They still could not believe it. Is this a continued statement of unbelief? Or is it a rhetorical expression of their amazement? They are being moved to faith, so a rhetorical force is more likely here.
Amazement is the common response to unusual activity: 1:63; 2:18; 4:22; 7:9; 8:25; 9:43; 11:14; 20:26.

Do you have anything here to eat? Eating would remove the idea that a phantom was present. Angelic spirits refused a meal in Judg 13:16 and Tob 12:19, but accepted it in Gen 18:8; 19:3 and Tob 6:6. (Tobit, a book of the OT Apocrypha, reflects views during the intertestamental period.)

verses.zh: 他们便给他一片烧鱼。（有古卷加：和一块蜜房。）
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] they gave him a piece of broiled fish,
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of Jesus’ request for food.

verses.zh: 他接过来，在他们面前吃了。
verses.en: and he took it and ate it in front of them.

verses.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「这就是我从前与你们同在之时所告诉你们的话说：摩西的律法、先知的书，和诗篇上所记的，凡指着我的话都必须应验。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he said to them, “These are my words that I spoke to you while I was still with you, that everything written about me[NOTE:2] in the law of Moses and the prophets and the psalms[NOTE:3] must be fulfilled.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Everything written about me. The divine plan, events, and scripture itself are seen here as being one.
For a similar threefold division of the OT scriptures, see the prologue to Sirach, lines 8-10, and from Qumran, the epilogue to 4QMMT, line 10.

verses.zh: 于是耶稣开他们的心窍，使他们能明白圣经，
verses.en: Then he opened their minds so they could understand the scriptures,[NOTE:1]
notes: Luke does not mention specific texts here, but it is likely that many of the scriptures he mentioned elsewhere in Luke-Acts would have been among those he had in mind.

verses.zh: 又对他们说：「照经上所写的，基督必受害，第三日从死里复活，
verses.en: and said to them, “Thus it stands written that the Christ[NOTE:1] would suffer[NOTE:2] and would rise from the dead on the third day,
notes: Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”

Three Greek infinitives are the key to this summary: (1) to suffer, (2) to rise, and (3) to be preached. The Christ (Messiah) would be slain, would be raised, and a message about repentance would go out into all the world as a result. All of this was recorded in the scripture. The remark shows the continuity between Jesus’ ministry, the scripture, and what disciples would be doing as they declared the Lord risen.

verses.zh: 并且人要奉他的名传悔改、赦罪的道，从耶路撒冷起直传到万邦。
verses.en: and repentance[NOTE:1] for the forgiveness of sins would be proclaimed[NOTE:2] in his name to all nations,[NOTE:3] beginning from Jerusalem.[NOTE:4]
notes: This repentance has its roots in declarations of the Old Testament. It is the Hebrew concept of a turning of direction.
Or “preached,” “announced.”
To all nations. The same Greek term (τὰ ἔθνη, ta ethnē) may be translated “the Gentiles” or “the nations.” The hope of God in Christ was for all the nations from the beginning.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.sn Beginning from Jerusalem. See Acts 2, which is where it all starts.

verses.zh: 你们就是这些事的见证。
verses.en: You are witnesses[NOTE:1] of these things.
notes: You are witnesses. This becomes a key concept of testimony in Acts. See Acts 1:8.

verses.zh: 我要将我父所应许的降在你们身上，你们要在城里等候，直到你们领受从上头来的能力。」
verses.en: And look, I am sending you[NOTE:1] what my Father promised.[NOTE:2] But stay in the city[NOTE:3] until you have been clothed with power[NOTE:4] from on high.”
notes: Grk “sending on you.”

Grk “the promise of my Father,” with τοῦ πατρός (tou patros) translated as a subjective genitive. This is a reference to the Holy Spirit and looks back to how one could see Messiah had come with the promise of old (Luke 3:15-18). The promise is rooted in Jer 31:31 and Ezek 36:26.
The city refers to Jerusalem.

Until you have been clothed with power refers to the coming of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost. What the Spirit supplies is enablement. See Luke 12:11-12; 21:12-15. The difference the Spirit makes can be seen in Peter (compare Luke 22:54-62 with Acts 2:14-41).

verses.zh: 耶稣领他们到伯大尼的对面，就举手给他们祝福。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] led them out as far as Bethany,[NOTE:3] and lifting up his hands, he blessed them.
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Bethany was village on the Mount of Olives about 2 mi (3 km) from Jerusalem; see John 11:1, 18.

verses.zh: 正祝福的时候，他就离开他们，被带到天上去了。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] during the blessing[NOTE:2] he departed[NOTE:3] and was taken up into heaven.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “And it happened that while.” The introductory phrase ἐγένετο (egeneto, “it happened that”), common in Luke (69 times) and Acts (54 times), is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.
Grk “while he blessed them.”
Grk “he departed from them.”

There is great debate whether this event equals Acts 1:9-11 so that Luke has telescoped something here that he describes in more detail later. The text can be read in this way because the temporal marker in v. 50 is vague. tn For the translation of ἀνεφέρετο (anephereto) as “was taken up” see BDAG 75 s.v. ἀναφέρω 1.tc The reference to the ascension (“and was taken up into heaven”) is lacking in א* D it sys, but it is found in P75 and the rest of the ms tradition. The authenticity of the statement here seems to be presupposed in Acts 1:2, for otherwise it is difficult to account for Luke’s reference to the ascension there. For a helpful discussion, see TCGNT 162-63.

verses.zh: 他们就拜他，大大地欢喜，回耶路撒冷去，
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] they worshiped[NOTE:2] him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,[NOTE:3]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the result of Jesus’ ascension and the concluding summary of Luke’s Gospel.
The reference to worship is lacking in the Western ms D, its last major omission in this Gospel.
Joy is another key theme for Luke: 1:14; 2:10; 8:13; 10:17; 15:7, 10; 24:41.

verses.zh: 常在殿里称颂　神。
verses.en: and were continually in the temple courts[NOTE:1] blessing[NOTE:2] God.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “in the temple.”sn Luke’s gospel story proper ends where it began, in the temple courts (Luke 1:4-22). The conclusion is open-ended because the story continues in Acts with what happened from Jerusalem onwards, once the promise of the Father (v. 49) came.

The Western text (D it) has αἰνοῦντες (ainountes, “praising”) here, while the Alexandrian mss (P75 א B C* L) have εὐλογοῦντες (eulogountes, “blessing”). Most mss, especially the later Byzantine mss, evidently combine these two readings with αἰνοῦντες καὶ εὐλογοῦντες (A C2 W Θ Ψ ƒ1,13 33 M lat). It is more difficult to decide between the two earlier readings. Internal arguments can go either way, but what seems decisive in this instance are the superior witnesses for εὐλογοῦντες.

The majority of Greek mss, some of which are significant witnesses (A B C2 Θ Ψ ƒ13 M lat), add “Amen” to note the Gospel’s end. Such a conclusion is routinely added by scribes to NT books because a few of these books originally had such an ending (cf. Rom 16:27; Gal 6:18; Jude 25). A majority of Greek witnesses have the concluding ἀμήν in every NT book except Acts, James, and 3 John (and even in these books, ἀμήν is found in some witnesses). It is thus a predictable variant. Further, since significant witnesses lack the word (P75 א C* D L W 1 33 it co), it is evidently not original.
